title: The SQL Injection Bug Hiding in Plain Java Code
description:
One string concatenation is all it takes for a login form to leak your entire users table. This Short breaks down how SQL injection actually works in Java, and the one-line fix (PreparedStatement / Spring Data parameter binding) that closes it for good. Full lesson covers the rest of the OWASP Top 10 -- XSS, CSRF, and secrets management.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/05-security-best-practices/

#Shorts

beats.narration: This one line of Java code lets a hacker log in as literally any user -- and it compiles just fine.
Concatenate user input straight into a SQL query, and a single crafted string turns your WHERE clause into something that's always true -- returning every row, including passwords.
The fix is one keyword: PreparedStatement. It binds your input strictly as data, never as part of the SQL itself.
And if you're using Spring Data's @Query with named parameters like this, you're already safe -- it binds the same way under the hood.

display.code:
@Query("SELECT u FROM User u WHERE u.email = :email")
Optional<User> findByEmail(@Param("email") String email);

beats.narration: That one swap is the difference between a secure app and a headline. Full security checklist -- XSS, CSRF, secrets, all of it -- is linked below.
